newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends sharply stronger on NYMEX rally.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends sharply stronger on NYMEX rally.

text.p: IPE January Brent crude oil ended Monday almost one dollar stronger after NYMEX gasoline led a late price rally. Some brokers said the rally was triggered following news that Mexico's three crude shipping ports were closed due to high winds while others pointed to shortcovering supported by good product demand in New York Harbour.
"The rally is led by (NYMEX) gasoline which broke up on news of the port closures. They are taking almost 1.5 million barrels of crude per day out of the market, one broker said.

"A lot of Americans came in today with relatively square books and were looking to see which way this market should go. Once it started to go up no-one would dare to sell it and it went for the moon," another commented.
January Brent closed up 85 cents at $23.63 a barrel.
The Jan Brent/WTI spread widened out around 20 cents to $1.15-20 a barrel.
"This move may have been overdone but there is good fundamental strength," another broker said.
Mexico's three crude shipping ports were closed on Monday as a cold front blew winds of up to 50 kilometers per hour along the Gulf of Mexico, port captains said.
NYMEX gasoline led the rally and large volume buy stops were hit as prices broke upwards.

U.S. brokers also saw support coming from the continuing strike at Elf Aquitaines three French refineries as the arbitrage from Europe to the U.S. was still open and the strike could lower U.S. imports.

December IPE gas oil closed earlier down some 50 cents at $219.75 a tonne. Based on the Brent crude and NYMEX heating oil closing prices the gas oil contract should open on Tuesday up some $7-8 a tonne but brokers said this was unrealistic.
"It will open stronger but $7 to $8 is too much. We will have to wait and see," one added.
